meta.title: Transformative Community Projects — Conceptual Knowledge Graph
meta.description: Thematic and theoretical structure. Reusable across projects.

nodes.label: Transformative Community Projects
nodes.description: An integrated model for sustainable forms of learning, working, and living. Not a single reform but the interaction of multiple variables in an overall context.

nodes.label: Diagnosis — What's Wrong
nodes.description: Analysis of contemporary society's structural problems that motivate the project.

nodes.label: Alienation in Work Life
nodes.description: Functionalized work yields experiences lacking professional self-realization. Competition, indifference, and alienation frame the work-life experience.

quotes.text: The functionalized world of work yields human experiences that often lack professional self-realization.
Many would rather guard the Wall of Ice in Game of Thrones, or be part of Winterfell, than have to look for a place in our society, which is often experienced as indifferent and functionalist.

nodes.label: Crisis of the School System
nodes.description: Increasing numbers of youth not fitting into schools. Male students at high risk. Declining attractiveness of teaching profession. Schools as places of mere safekeeping.

quotes.text: More and more children and young people are not fitting into the school system and reacting with behaviors that are considered problematic, and a growing group is not even learning the basics there.
It is not a matter of developing ever more precise diagnostic instruments and pedagogical interventions... what matters is that they grow up differently and better, right from the start.

nodes.label: Social Fragmentation
nodes.description: Disintegration of families, unconnected coexistence of communities, lives in escapist virtual worlds. Loss of cohesion, meaning, significance.

quotes.text: There is no narrative that would effectively hold together this society, which is now primarily functionalist. There is no meaningful narrative, nothing that motivates us as a society as a whole.

nodes.label: Society of Control (Deleuze)
nodes.description: Deleuze's analysis: control systems play a dominant role, individual freedom diminishes. Manifests in educational institutions. Central framing across all three books.

nodes.label: Skilled Worker Shortage
nodes.description: Shortage in geriatric care, teaching, trades. Lateral entrants without preparation. Unsustainable cycle.

nodes.label: Philosophical Foundations
nodes.description: The intellectual traditions and thinkers informing the project.

nodes.label: Communitarianism
nodes.description: Social embedding without collectivist coercion. Decline of values and solidarity under neoliberalism. Preserves individual freedom while emphasizing social community.

nodes.label: O'Donohue — Belonging & Thresholds
nodes.description: Irish philosopher. Belonging as social and emotional connectedness. Thresholds as biographical/spiritual transitions. Appreciation of inner richness each person brings.

quotes.text: In the writings of the Irish philosopher John O'Donohue, thresholds hold the special meaning of consciously entering and exiting from something. They can also denote certain biographical or spiritual developments.

nodes.label: Fromm — Being vs. Having
nodes.description: Being makes you happier than having. Questioning fixation on material accumulation under capitalism.

nodes.label: Strong Democracy (Barber)
nodes.description: Participatory politics for a new age. Active citizenship beyond representative democracy.

nodes.label: Person-Centered Philosophy
nodes.description: Rogers' person-centered approach. Constructive shaping of human relationships. Genuine inclusion of each person.

nodes.label: Resonance (Rosa)
nodes.description: Significant resonance experience as fundamental for human development. Connection vs. alienation.

nodes.label: Social Sculpture (Beuys)
nodes.description: Joseph Beuys' concept — society itself as an artwork shaped by everyone. Referenced in De Gruyter volume.
references: De Gruyter 2025, Ch. 'Soziale Plastik im Sinne von Joseph Beuys'

nodes.label: Pillars — The Model
nodes.description: The five key elements of the transformative community project model.

nodes.label: Active Civil Society
nodes.description: Citizens taking social, economic, and educational responsibility. Not waiting for state support. The post-institutional era.

quotes.text: We should now usher in the post-institutional era. The state will not fix it alone, nor should it.
We are not waiting for state support and financing, but we are doing it from our own resources.

nodes.label: Work, Income & Work-Life Balance
nodes.description: Rethinking labor. Manual and intellectual work equally valued. Deceleration. Self-determination.

nodes.label: Unconditional Basic Income
nodes.description: Not redistribution from middle to bottom, but incentive for entrepreneurial activity and social responsibility. Dismantles welfare bureaucracy. Frees tax money for projects.

quotes.text: It can never be the case that a certain social group, which is usually active in the hamster wheel of 9-5 jobs, generates the basic income for another social group. If so, then everyone gets it.

nodes.label: Meaningful Labor
nodes.description: Roofers and philosophers, carpenters and educators working side by side. Manual and practical work equally valued alongside intellectual work. Craftsmanship rediscovered.

quotes.text: Those were wonderful days, when the value of practical, hands-on work became impressively visible and tangible.

nodes.label: Deceleration & Slow Living
nodes.description: Reduced mobility, more time for each other, healthier pace. Action and contemplation in balance.

quotes.text: But there should also be ease, not just work and no play. Reading popular fiction is part of it; so is listening to music on your headphones, lounging on the Wooden Deck and just closing our eyes or watching the clouds go by.

nodes.label: Learning & Education
nodes.description: Self-directed, community-oriented learning as alternative to institutional schooling.

nodes.label: Self-Designed Compulsory Education
nodes.description: Transform compulsory school attendance into self-directed mandatory education. Grades and certificates replaced by university entrance exams. Thousands of extracurricular projects needed.

quotes.text: Transforming compulsory school attendance into self-directed mandatory education would spur society enormously by opening the door to a new kind of social, economic, and cultural development.

nodes.label: Experiential Education
nodes.description: Learning by doing. Dewey, Hahn, Weikart's HighScope model. Action-oriented, nature-embedded. The farm as classroom.

quotes.text: If I have seen with my own eyes and experienced first-hand anywhere in the world what an activity- and project-oriented, creativity-driven and innovative, holistic approach to education should be, this was it.

nodes.label: Community-Oriented Learning
nodes.description: Intergenerational learning. Diverse role models, especially male presence. Cooperative skill-building. Children grow up with multiple adult caregivers.

nodes.label: Youth Journeying — Wanderjahre
nodes.description: Adolescents move between projects — farm to mill to urban workshop. Self-determined years of exploration. Reimagined apprenticeship. Documented in De Gruyter as 'Wanderjahre als Zeit des Lernens'.

nodes.label: Community Leadership (University Subject)
nodes.description: Proposed new university discipline combining economics, sociology, architecture, education, creative arts — training people to lead transformative community projects.

nodes.label: Entrepreneurship
nodes.description: Community-based enterprise. Reviving abandoned properties. Commons-based resource sharing.

nodes.label: Community-Based Enterprise
nodes.description: Entrepreneurial communities in structurally weak areas. Start-ups, workshops, services founded on basic income stability.

nodes.label: The Commons & Commoning
nodes.description: Shared resources, jointly managed. Medieval pastures to modern commons projects. Managing resources together rather than competing.

nodes.label: Rural Revitalization
nodes.description: Abandoned farms, chateaux, train stations, dairies in East Germany as opportunities. Thousands of vacant properties waiting.

quotes.text: Scattered throughout Anhalt, like other regions in eastern Germany, are numerous abandoned properties just waiting for people to get together to make something out of them.

nodes.label: Creative Class
nodes.description: Florida's creative class discourse applied to rural transformation. Creativity as driver of community development.

nodes.label: Community Building
nodes.description: Building diverse, democratic, sustainable communities. Inclusive of gender, disability, age, culture, tradition, religion, language.

nodes.label: Radical Inclusion
nodes.description: Elders, people with disabilities, diverse cultural backgrounds. Reducing expensive care facilities through community integration.

nodes.label: Intergenerational Living
nodes.description: Multiple generations learning from each other. More adult caregivers per child. Male role models present.

nodes.label: Neighborly Structures & Mutual Aid
nodes.description: Organic cooperation with village neighbors. Tractor help exchanged for field access. Firewood for services. Old patterns renewed.

quotes.text: A village farmer helps to pull out fence posts with his tractor, and in return, this farmer cultivates fields on this property.

nodes.label: Transformation
nodes.description: The binding philosophy — seeing oneself as part of economic, social, cultural, and ecological transformation.

nodes.label: Economic Transformation
nodes.description: From capitalist accumulation toward commons-based, community-embedded economies. Reduced academization. Money redirected from bureaucracy to people.

nodes.label: Social Transformation
nodes.description: Rebuilding social cohesion, belonging, identity-promoting narratives. Creative disorder (Sennett) rather than top-down planning.

nodes.label: Cultural Transformation
nodes.description: Heritage preservation, Polish-German exchange, literature, music, crafts as cultural renewal. Emotional and social geographies in literature.

nodes.label: Ecological Transformation
nodes.description: Ecological building materials, organic farming, reduced mobility, biodiversity, climate-positive living. Green economy.

nodes.label: Safeguards & Critiques
nodes.description: Honest engagement with risks, criticisms, and necessary protections.

nodes.label: Democratic Oversight
nodes.description: Government agencies must oversee projects. Human rights guaranteed. Transparency, accessibility, financial disclosure. No indoctrination.

nodes.label: GDR Mistrust of Commons
nodes.description: In German society, mistrust of commons concepts recalls GDR socialism. Must be addressed openly.

nodes.label: Risk of Exploitation
nodes.description: Critics connect idea to abuse of power (e.g. Colonia Dignidad). Projects must prohibit conditioning, manipulation, subjugation.

nodes.label: Capitalist Mindset Persistence
nodes.description: Klien (2019): people who long for self-created work can still be strongly influenced by capitalist thinking. Need to learn to release mental pressure.
